source.title: Probing Large Language Model Hidden States for Adverse Drug Reaction Knowledge
source.authors: J. Berkowitz; D. Weissenbacher; A. Srinivasan; N. Friedrich; J. M. Acitores Cortina; S. Kivelson; G. G. Hernandez; N. Tatonetti

record.tranche_reason: The study uses pretrained sparse autoencoders to extract features for ADR classification, but does not test the neuron-pole interpretability claims or the proposed explanation tests.
record.gate_note: The study reports a manual annotation of SAE-identified features, but this is not a measurement of the share of interpretable neuron poles. ADR classification results and comparisons of SAE features with raw activations do not test the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study uses pretrained Gemma Scope SAEs as a tool to build ADR classifiers and reports classifier AUCs. It never audits the model's own neurons or neuron poles. It does not score neuron explanations by simulation, and it does not test explanations against where neurons fire. The one interpretability figure is a brief manual annotation of SAE features (46.6% 'somewhat science related'). That concerns SAE dictionary features, not neurons, and measures topical relevance to science rather than whether a unit has one main job.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct in substance. The authors conclude that Gemma Scope SAE features from Gemma-2-9b-it drug-name embeddings support strong linear ADR classification (AUC 0.90–0.96). This shows no significant difference from MLPs on raw activations and beats direct prompting, so SAEs keep the essential information while simplifying models. They also note the retained features show only partial monosemanticity.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Gemma Scope SAEs on Gemma-2-9b-it activations and trains logistic classifiers for ADR prediction; it does not audit neuron poles or test explanations on held-out activating examples.

fits_no_version.finding: In a brief manual annotation, 46.6% of the SAE features retained by L1 ADR classifiers were judged 'somewhat science related'. The authors call this partial monosemanticity and give an example: feature 91141 (footwear/ankle) appears in the acute kidney injury model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features selected by sparse probes for a biomedical task are often not topically related to that domain, though this does not show the features themselves are polysemantic.

record.problems: The paper gives little detail about the manual annotation, including annotation criteria and annotator count. The 46.6% figure concerns selected SAE features, not all neurons or neuron poles.
record.rows_left_out: ADR classification AUCs, generative predictions, and SAE-versus-raw-activation comparisons are omitted because they do not measure the claim's neuron interpretability or explanation-prediction outcomes.

untested.parts: Share of Qwen3-32B neuron poles with one job, two jobs or not yet understood.
Neuron interpretability shares in other models or at other scales.
Effect of architecture, regularization or tools on the share of interpretable neurons.
Neuron-based attribution graphs without a replacement model.
Whether explanations from activating examples predict where a neuron fires.

record.verdict_notes: The study is a medRxiv preprint applying SAEs to pharmacovigilance. It does not concern neuron-level interpretability shares. 'Partial monosemanticity' is the authors' gloss on a science-relatedness annotation, and it should not be read as evidence about V1, V2 or V6.

versions.untested_parts: The share of Qwen3-32B neuron poles with one or two jobs, or not understood.
Interpretability shares across models, architectures, or scale.
The interpretation of classic polysemantic neurons and recursive generalization.
Whether architecture, regularization, or tools change the share of interpretable neurons.
Whether attribution graphs using a model's own neurons explain its behaviour without a trained replacement model.
Whether explanations fit to activating examples fail to predict where neurons fire.
Automated scoring of neuron explanations on new text.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9b-it
rows.operation_detail: Manual annotation of features identified by SAEs

conditions.value: SAE-identified features; selection details not stated

rows.measure: Share of identified features judged somewhat science related
rows.note: The authors describe this as partial monosemanticity. It is an aggregate annotation result, not a neuron-pole interpretability rate.
rows.check: The subject is SAE features, not Gemma-2-9b-it neurons. The features are those kept by L1 logistic regression, which makes this a selection-based measure. The construct is 'science related', not monosemanticity or explanation quality. Annotation criteria and annotator count are not stated. The row may be kept as descriptive, but it bears on no version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
